mainTopic: The colors of impure blood in a woman: the משנה's list, the source that some blood is pure, and how the four types from 'דמיה דמיה' fit the משנה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion. When a woman does not know what her miscarried piece looked like, רבי יהודה follows the majority of such pieces and rules her impure, while רבנן do not rely on that majority. Then a new משנה lists five colors of blood that make a woman impure: red, black, crocus, earth-water and diluted wine. It brings disputes over extra colors, between בית שמאי and בית הלל and about green blood, and then defines each color with an exact sample. The גמרא asks how we know any blood from a woman is pure, and learns it from the פסוק 'between blood and blood.' It tests that proof against 'between נגע and נגע' and shows that in נגעים of people, houses and clothing there are real disputes a זקן ממרא could argue about. With blood, there would be nothing to argue about unless some blood is pure. רבי אבהו then learns from the double word 'דמיה' that there are four impure types, and רבי חנינא explains that black is really red that went dark. The amud ends by asking how בית הלל differ from the תנא קמא, and the answer begins: there is a practical difference between them.

steps.title: Following the majority of miscarried pieces
steps.stepSummary: When a woman does not know what the miscarried piece looked like, רבי יהודה follows the majority of pieces, which are impure-blood colored. רבנן do not use this majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she does not know what she miscarried, רבי יהודה holds that we follow the majority of pieces, and most pieces are one of the four kinds of impure blood. רבנן hold that we do not say 'follow the majority of pieces.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier answer. It explains the case that was being excluded: a woman who does not know what her miscarried piece looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה uses a statistical majority: most miscarried pieces have an impure blood color, so this woman is treated as definitely impure. רבנן reject using this kind of majority, so she is not treated as definitely impure based on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after the majority. Decide an unknown case based on what usually happens.
Pieces of flesh that were miscarried.
She miscarried.
We do not say. The principle is rejected.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה follows the majority of miscarried pieces to rule the woman impure. רבנן do not rely on that majority.

phrases.english: and she does not know what she miscarried,
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
Follow the majority of pieces,

phrases.aramaic: וְרוֹב חֲתִיכוֹת שֶׁל אַרְבַּע מִינֵי דָּמִים הָוְיָין.
phrases.english: and the majority of pieces are of the four kinds of blood.
phrases.notes: He means the colors of blood that make a woman impure.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: זִיל בָּתַר רוֹב חֲתִיכוֹת לָא אָמְרִינַן.
phrases.english: We do not say: follow the majority of pieces.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: זִיל בָּתַר רוֹב חֲתִיכוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer that began before this section, explaining which case was being excluded.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the specific opinion being excluded, which is רבי יהודה's use of a majority.
steps.terutzMaskana: The excluded case is the unknown miscarriage, where רבי יהודה rules impurity by majority and רבנן disagree.

steps.title: Five colors of impure blood
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists the five colors of blood that make a woman impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five kinds of blood are impure in a woman: red, black, like the bright crocus, like earth-water, and like diluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the five blood colors that make a woman impure as a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every discharge counts as impure blood. Only these five colors do. The משנה will define some of them shortly.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure bloods. Blood colors that make a woman a נדה.
The bright part of the crocus (saffron) flower.
Water mixed with red earth.
Diluted wine (wine mixed with water).

steps.whatToRemember: There are five impure blood colors: red, black, crocus, earth-water, and diluted wine.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Five kinds of blood are impure in a woman:
the red, and the black,
and like the bright color of the crocus,
and like water of earth, and like diluted wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה דָּמִים טְמֵאִים בָּאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five blood colors are impure: red, black, crocus-colored, earth-water, and diluted wine.

steps.title: Two more colors in dispute
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי add two more impure colors. בית הלל say they are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: also blood like fenugreek water and like the juice of roasted meat is impure. בית הלל rule these pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a מחלוקת. בית שמאי want to add two more colors to the list, and בית הלל disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, the list is really seven colors. According to בית הלל, these two lighter colors do not make a woman impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Water in which fenugreek was soaked.
Roasted meat. Here it refers to the juice that drips from it.
They rule it pure.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אַף כְּמֵימֵי תִלְתָּן,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: also like fenugreek water,
and like the liquid of roasted meat,
and Beit Hillel rule them pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אַף כְּמֵימֵי תִלְתָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a dispute about expanding the list of five.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי treat fenugreek-water and roast-meat-juice colors as impure. בית הלל treat them as pure.

steps.title: Green blood
steps.stepSummary: עקביא בן מהללאל rules green blood impure. חכמים rule it pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Green blood: עקביא בן מהללאל rules it impure, and the חכמים rule it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings another מחלוקת, this time about green-colored blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עקביא בן מהללאל counts green as an impure blood color. חכמים do not.

keyTerms.meaning: Green (or a yellowish-green color).
Rules it impure.

phrases.english: The green: Akavya ben Mahalalel rules it impure,
and the Rabbis rule it pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיָּרוֹק — עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל מְטַמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another dispute about a color that is not on the list of five.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עקביא בן מהללאל rules green blood impure. חכמים rule it pure.

steps.title: Does green blood count as a liquid?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says that even if green blood is not impure as a stain, it still counts as a liquid that makes food able to become impure. רבי יוסי says it counts as neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: even if it does not make her impure as a stain, it makes food susceptible to impurity as a liquid. רבי יוסי says: neither this way nor that way.
steps.whatsHappening: Two more תנאים give their views on the green blood. The question is whether it has any status as blood at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says that even if green blood does not make a woman impure, since it is still blood it is one of the liquids that can prepare food to become impure. רבי יוסי says green blood is not blood in either sense.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment or body.
A liquid. Certain liquids (like blood) make food able to become impure.
Neither this way nor that way.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying green blood makes the woman a נדה. He only says it acts as a liquid that prepares food to become impure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said: If it does not make impure as a stain,
it makes impure as a liquid.
phrases.notes: He means it makes food able to become impure, like the other liquids, such as water and blood.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: לֹא כָּךְ וְלֹא כָּךְ.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: Neither this way nor that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִם אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of green blood with a further dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: green blood counts as a liquid that makes food susceptible to impurity. רבי יוסי: it counts as neither impure blood nor such a liquid.

steps.title: Defining red, black, and crocus
steps.stepSummary: The משנה defines the colors: red is like wound blood, black is like חרת, and crocus means its brightest part.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is red? Like blood of a wound. Black? Like חרת. Darker than that is impure, and lighter than that is pure. Like crocus? Like its brightest part.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now starts explaining exactly what each impure color looks like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each color gets a real-world comparison so it can be judged. For black, the משנה also sets a limit: darker than חרת is impure, and lighter than חרת is pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood from a wound.
A black substance used as the standard for the black color.
Deeper (darker).
Lighter (faded).
The clearest, brightest part.

phrases.english: What is red? Like the blood of a wound;
black: like ḥeret;
deeper than that is impure,
lighter than that is pure;
and like the bright crocus: like its brightest part;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיזֶהוּ אָדוֹם — כְּדַם הַמַּכָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of five and begins defining its colors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Red is like wound blood. Black is like חרת, where darker is impure and lighter is pure. Crocus means its brightest part.

steps.title: Defining earth-water and diluted wine colors
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its definitions. 'Earth-water' means water flooded over soil from the בקעת בית כרם. 'Diluted wine' means two parts water to one part wine from the שרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'like earth-water' mean? Earth from the בקעת בית כרם, with water poured over it until the water floats on top. What does 'like diluted wine' mean? Two parts water and one part wine, using wine from the שרון region.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the list from the last step and defines the last two impure colors exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each color is tied to one specific real-world sample, a certain soil and a certain wine at a fixed mix. This lets a רב compare blood against a clear standard instead of guessing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Earth-water': water mixed with reddish soil
The Beit Kerem valley, the source of the soil used as the color standard
Diluted, meaning wine mixed with water
Wine from the Sharon region

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's five impure colors are each matched to an exact sample: wound blood, חרת, the brightest part of crocus, בית כרם earth-water, and diluted wine from the שרון.

phrases.english: And 'like earth-water' means:
soil from the Beit Kerem valley,
with water flooded over it so it floats on top;
and 'like diluted wine' means:
two parts water and one part wine,
from the wine of the Sharon region.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְמֵימֵי אֲדָמָה מִבִּקְעַת בֵּית כֶּרֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the color definitions begun in step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Earth-water means בית כרם soil covered with water. Diluted wine means two parts water to one part wine from the שרון.

steps.title: How do we know some blood from a woman is pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for a source that a woman can have pure blood. Maybe all blood from her is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know that a woman can have pure blood? Maybe any blood that comes from her is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source behind the משנה's whole idea. The משנה listed only certain colors as impure, which implies other blood is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By listing specific impure colors, the משנה assumes some blood from a woman is pure. The גמרא wants a source for that assumption. Without one, we might say every kind of blood makes her impure.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
From where do we know? A request for a source
Pure blood, blood that does not make the woman impure
Perhaps, maybe

phrases.english: GEMARA:
From where do we know that there is pure blood in a woman?
Perhaps all blood
that comes out of her is impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן דְּאִיכָּא דָּם טָהוֹר בָּאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא's first question about it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that some blood from a woman is pure

steps.title: The פסוק 'between blood and blood'
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא בר יוסף quotes רבי אושעיא. The פסוק says 'between blood and blood,' which means between pure blood and impure blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא בר יוסף said in the name of רבי אושעיא: The פסוק says, 'If a matter of judgment is too hard for you, between blood and blood.' This means between pure blood and impure blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a פסוק that speaks of judging 'between blood and blood.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every blood were impure, there would be nothing to judge between. The פסוק describes a hard decision between two kinds of blood. So some blood must be pure and some impure.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is too hard, too hidden to decide
Judgment, a ruling
Between blood and blood

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥama bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Oshaya said:
The verse says:
'If a matter of judgment is too hard for you,
phrases.notes: דברים 17:8

phrases.english: between blood and blood.'
This means between pure blood and impure blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אֲמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's 'between blood and blood' means between pure and impure blood, so pure blood exists.

steps.title: Then 'between נגע and נגע' should mean pure and impure too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the reading. The same פסוק says 'between נגע and נגע.' Read the same way, that would mean pure and impure נגעים, but there is no such thing as a pure נגע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, the same פסוק says 'between נגע and נגע.' Does that also mean between an impure נגע and a pure נגע? And if you say yes, is there really such a thing as a pure נגע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אושעיא's reading by using it on the next words of the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'blood and blood' means pure versus impure, then 'נגע and נגע' should mean the same. But by definition a נגע is a mark that makes a person impure. So the method seems to prove too much, and that casts doubt on the reading of 'blood and blood.'

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: if we accept your logic, look where it leads
A mark of צרעת on the skin
So too, the same here
Is there such a thing?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying there is no pure blood. It is testing whether this פסוק is a good source for it.

phrases.english: But if so,
'between נגע and נגע,'
phrases.notes: These words come from later in the same פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי בֵּין נֶגַע טָמֵא לְנֶגַע טָהוֹר?
phrases.english: does that also mean between an impure נגע and a pure נגע?
And if you say, yes, it does,
is there such a thing as a pure נגע?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה בֵּין נֶגַע לָנֶגַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading given in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's reading of 'between blood and blood' as pure versus impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Read the same way, 'between נגע and נגע' would mean pure versus impure נגעים, yet a pure נגע does not exist.

steps.title: The fully white case is not a pure נגע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible defense. Someone might point to 'it has all turned white, he is pure,' but that mark is called a בוהק, not a נגע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say there is a pure נגע, from the פסוק 'it has all turned white, he is pure,' that mark is called a בוהק, not a נגע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a defense before anyone can raise it. It strengthens the challenge from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a person whose whole body turned white is a case of a 'pure נגע.' The גמרא says that mark has a different name, בוהק, and is not a נגע at all. So the challenge stands: the word נגע always means an impure mark.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say: introduces a possible answer
Turned white, when the mark covers the whole body
A pale skin mark that does not make a person impure

steps.whyThisMatters: At this point the challenge stands. The גמרא must explain how 'blood and blood' can teach pure versus impure when 'נגע and נגע' cannot. Steps 13-20 work this out.

phrases.english: And if you say there is one, from:
'It has all turned white; he is pure,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:13

phrases.english: that mark is called a 'בוהק,' not a נגע!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא כֻּלּוֹ הָפַךְ לָבָן טָהוֹר הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible answer to the challenge in step 10
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the fully white case as an example of a pure נגע
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The fully white mark is called a בוהק, not a נגע, so it is not a pure נגע.

steps.title: A new reading: different kinds of impure marks, and so different kinds of impure blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'between נגע and נגע' means between נגעים on people, houses and clothing, all impure. Then 'between blood and blood' could mean נדה blood and זיבה blood, both impure, and this knocks out the proof for pure blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means between נגעים of a person, of houses and of clothing, and all of them are impure. Here too, it means between נדה blood and זיבה blood, and all of them are impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different reading of 'between נגע and נגע' that works with no pure נגע at all. It then uses the same reading for 'between blood and blood,' so the proof that a woman can have pure blood is gone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 10 the problem was that there is no pure נגע. Here the גמרא says the פסוק is not comparing pure with impure. It is comparing different kinds that are all impure. Read this way, 'blood and blood' means two kinds of impure blood, נדה and זיבה, so we lose the source for pure blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks of צרעת on a person's skin
Marks of צרעת on the walls of a house
Marks of צרעת on clothing
Blood of a woman's regular monthly period
Blood that comes outside her regular days, making her a זבה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final view. It is a reading suggested to undo רבי אושעיא's proof, and the very next step pushes back on it.

phrases.english: Rather: between the marks of a person
phrases.notes: He means the words 'between נגע and נגע' in the same פסוק (דברים 17:8).

phrases.english: and the marks of houses and the marks of clothing,
and they are all impure.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: בֵּין דַּם נִדָּה לְדַם זִיבָה,
phrases.english: Here too: between נדה blood and זיבה blood,
and they are all impure!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בֵּין נִגְעֵי אָדָם לְנִגְעֵי בָתִּים וּלְנִגְעֵי בְגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 11 shows 'all white' is a בוהק and not a נגע, the גמרא offers another way to read 'נגע and נגע' that also cancels the proof for pure blood.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אושעיא's proof (step 9) that 'between blood and blood' means pure and impure blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'נגע and נגע' means different kinds of impure marks, then 'blood and blood' can mean different kinds of impure blood, and the פסוק says nothing about pure blood.

steps.title: Pushing back: with נגעים there is room for a real argument
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the new reading. With נגעים of a person there is real room for a זקן ממרא to argue with the רבנן, for example in the dispute of רבי יהושע and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this? It makes sense there, because a rebellious elder and the רבנן can argue about נגעים of a person, as in the dispute of רבי יהושע and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says 'What kind of comparison is this?' and starts to show why the new reading of 'blood and blood' does not work. It points out that with נגעים of a person there is a real halachic argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים 17:8 lists areas where a hard case goes to the בית דין, and where a זקן ממרא could rule against it. So each area named must hold a real halachic argument. For נגעים of a person there is one, the dispute of רבי יהושע and the רבנן. The next step quotes it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is this?' A way of saying the comparison does not hold
'Granted' or 'it makes sense.' It sets up a contrast with another case
A rebellious elder, a sage who rules in practice against the בית דין הגדול
A dispute between sages

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the rule for the rest of the section. Each area in the פסוק must contain a real argument that a זקן ממרא could have with the בית דין.

phrases.english: What is this?
Granted, there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of נגעים.

phrases.english: there is room to disagree
[a rebellious elder and the Rabbis] about the marks of a person,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, and they make clear who is arguing here.

phrases.english: in the dispute of Rabbi Yehoshua and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי? בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It answers the reading from step 12 by showing that the comparison between נגעים and blood does not hold.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading of 'blood and blood' as נדה blood and זיבה blood.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק is about areas where a זקן ממרא can argue with the בית דין. With נגעים there are real disputes, so the new reading fits there, but the same comparison does not automatically fit blood.

steps.title: The source: the doubt about which came first, the white hair or the bright spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. If the bright spot came before the white hair, the person is impure. If the white hair came first, he is pure. In a doubt, the רבנן say impure, while רבי יהושע says 'dull,' which רבה explains means pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: If the bright spot came before the white hair, he is impure. If the white hair came before the bright spot, he is pure. In a doubt, he is impure. רבי יהושע says: 'dull.' And רבה said: it is like a dull mark, and he is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה that shows the dispute of רבי יהושע and the רבנן about נגעים of a person. This backs up the claim in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A white hair only makes a person impure if it grew inside the bright spot after the spot appeared. When no one knows which came first, the רבנן rule impure. רבי יהושע rules pure, and רבה explains that he treats the mark like a dull one, which is not a sign of impurity. This is a real argument, so a זקן ממרא could rule against the בית דין here.

keyTerms.meaning: A bright, snow-white spot on the skin, a main type of נגע
White hair inside the spot, a sign of impurity
A case of doubt
Dull or faded. A mark that is not bright enough to make a person impure

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: אִם בַּהֶרֶת קוֹדֵם לְשֵׂעָר לָבָן
phrases.english: As we learned: if the bright spot came before the white hair
he is impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם שֵׂעָר לָבָן קוֹדֵם לַבַּהֶרֶת — טָהוֹר,
phrases.english: and if the white hair came before the bright spot, he is pure,
if there is a doubt, he is impure,
and Rabbi Yehoshua says: dull.
And Rabbah said: it is dull, and he is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: אִם בַּהֶרֶת קוֹדֵם לְשֵׂעָר לָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It gives the actual source for the dispute about נגעים of a person that step 13 mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a real halachic argument about נגעים of a person.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in נגעים (4:11): the doubt about which came first, the white hair or the bright spot.

steps.title: House marks also have an argument: the minimum size and place of the mark
steps.stepSummary: With נגעים of houses there is also a real argument. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says a house is impure only if the mark is the size of two beans, on two stones, on two walls in a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: With נגעים of houses there is a dispute like this one between רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון and the רבנן. As we learned: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says a house is never impure unless the mark is seen at the size of two split beans, on two stones, on two walls, in a corner. It must be two beans long and one bean wide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows a second area, נגעים of houses, where the sages really argue. It quotes the משנה with רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's strict requirements for a house to become impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון needs a large mark that spreads across two stones on two different walls meeting in a corner. The רבנן do not require this, so it is a real dispute. A זקן ממרא could rule against the בית דין here too, and this supports the point that each area in the פסוק holds real arguments.

keyTerms.meaning: A split bean, used as a measure of size
Walls
A corner, where two walls meet
Its length and its width

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא is showing that in every kind of נגע there are real disputes where a זקן ממרא could rule against the בית דין, because that is what the פסוק in דברים 17:8 is about.

phrases.english: With the marks of houses
like this dispute
of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as we learned: Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says:
a house is never impure
until the mark is seen at the size of two split beans

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁנֵי אֲבָנִים בִּשְׁנֵי כְּותָלִים בְּקֶרֶן זָוִית,
phrases.english: on two stones, on two walls, in a corner,
its length is two split beans and its width is one split bean.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנִגְעֵי בָתִּים — כִּי הָא פְּלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the example for נגעים of a person (step 14), the גמרא gives a second example, for נגעים of houses.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a real halachic argument about נגעים of houses.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה in נגעים (12:3): רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's minimum size and place for a house mark.

steps.title: What is the source for the corner rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון requires the mark on a house to be in a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask where רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון gets his rule about houses from step 15. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 said a house is impure only if the mark is on two stones, on two walls, in a corner. That is a surprising requirement, so the גמרא wants to see the פסוק behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason? It asks for the source behind an opinion.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the opinion quoted in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק teaches that a house's mark must be in a corner.

steps.title: One wall that counts as two walls is a corner
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says both 'wall' and 'walls', so it must mean one spot that is like two walls, which is a corner.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written 'wall' and it is written 'walls.' Which wall is like two walls? You must say: this is a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The פסוק uses both the single word 'wall' and the plural 'walls', and only a corner fits both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'walls' seems to require two walls, but the single 'wall' seems to require one. A corner is one place where two walls meet, so it satisfies both words at once. This is the source for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, and it shows there is a real dispute about houses.

keyTerms.meaning: Wall (singular).
Walls (plural).
A corner, the place where two walls meet.
You must say. It brings the only answer that fits.

phrases.english: "Wall" is written, and "walls" is written.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:37. Both words appear in the same פסוק about a house's נגע.

phrases.english: Which is a wall that is like two walls?
You must say: this is a corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב ״קִיר״ וּכְתִיב ״קִירוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק's use of both 'wall' and 'walls' points to a corner, one wall that is like two.

steps.title: Clothing marks also have a real dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that נגעי בגדים also have room for argument, in the dispute between רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: With marks on clothing, there is the dispute of רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן. As it was taught: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס says: From where do we know that a mark which spreads over clothing is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: After people and houses, the גמרא shows that clothing also has a real dispute, so a זקן ממרא could argue there too. It brings רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס's question, which sets up his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the point from step 13: נגעים of people, houses and clothing all have real disputes. רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס holds that if a mark covers a whole garment, the garment is pure, just as with a person. The רבנן disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Marks of צרעת on clothing.
A dispute between sages.
Spreading, when the mark covers the whole item.
From where do we know? It asks for a source.

phrases.english: With marks on clothing,

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אַבְטוּלְמוֹס וְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: there is the dispute of Rabbi Yonatan ben Avtolemos and the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: He means a זקן ממרא could argue about this dispute, just as with people and houses.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אַבְטוּלְמוֹס אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yonatan ben Avtolemos says:
From where do we know that a spreading over clothing is pure?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנִגְעֵי בְגָדִים בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹנָתָן בֶּן אַבְטוּלְמוֹס וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of real disputes from steps 14 and 15, now for clothing.
steps.raayaObject: That נגעי בגדים also have room for a זקן ממרא to argue.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute of רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס and the רבנן.

steps.title: Learning clothing from a person with a גזרה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The same words, קרחת and גבחת, appear for clothing and for a person, so a mark that spreads over a whole garment makes it pure, just like a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'קרחת' and 'גבחת' are said about clothing, and 'קרחת' and 'גבחת' are said about a person. Just as there, if it spread over all of him he is pure, so too here, if it spread over all of it, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס gives his source. The same words are used for clothing and for a person, so the rule for a person carries over to clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזרה שוה, which links two topics through the same words in the תורה. For a person, a נגע that covers the entire body makes him pure (step 11's 'it has all turned white, he is pure'). The shared words carry that rule over to clothing, so a garment that is fully covered is also pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a rule from one topic to another because the תורה uses the same words in both.
A bare spot. For clothing it means worn on the inside; for a person it means a bald back of the head.
A bare spot. For clothing it means worn on the outside; for a person it means a bald forehead.
Just as there... so too here. This formula carries a rule over from one case to another.
It spread over all of it, so the mark covers the whole thing.

steps.whatToRemember: All three kinds of נגעים have real disputes: people (רבי יהושע and the רבנן), houses (רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's corner rule), and clothing (רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס's rule that a fully covered garment is pure).

phrases.english: "Karachat" and "gabachat" are said about clothing,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:55

phrases.english: and "karachat" and "gabachat" are said about a person.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 13:42

phrases.english: Just as there, if it spread over all of him, he is pure,
phrases.notes: 'There' means a person. See ויקרא 13:13.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן נָמֵי פָּרַח בְּכוּלּוֹ טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: so too here, if it spread over all of it, it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר ״קָרַחַת״ וְ״גַבַּחַת״ בַּבְּגָדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנין question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזרה שוה from the shared words קרחת and גבחת carries the rule from a person to clothing: if the mark covers the whole thing, it is pure.

steps.title: Without pure blood there would be nothing to argue about
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up its proof: with נגעים of people, houses and clothing there is room for argument, but with blood, if no blood were ever pure, there would be nothing for the זקן ממרא to argue about. So the פסוק must be hinting that some blood is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, if there is no pure blood, what would they argue about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the proof it has been building. It compares blood to the other cases it just showed and concludes that some blood must be pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13-19 showed that נגעים of people, houses and clothing each have real disputes, even though all the marks are impure. With blood, if every kind were impure, there would be no dispute possible about 'בין דם לדם'. The only way the פסוק makes sense is if there are pure kinds and impure kinds of blood to argue over.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure blood: blood from a woman that does not make her impure
About what do they argue?

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'בין דם לדם' teaches that a woman can see blood that is pure, not only blood that is impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole next discussion: if some blood is pure, we need to know which colors are pure and which are impure.

phrases.english: But here,
phrases.notes: Here means the case of blood, from the פסוק 'בין דם לדם'.

phrases.english: if there is no pure blood,
about what would they argue?
phrases.notes: They means the זקן ממרא and the סנהדרין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא, אִי דָּם טָהוֹר לֵיכָּא, בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the בשלמא argument begun in step 13. Since נגעים have real disputes (steps 14-19) but blood would not, blood must include a pure kind.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since there must be something to argue about, there must be a type of woman's blood that is pure.

steps.title: How do we know which colors are pure and which are impure
steps.stepSummary: Now that we know some blood is pure, the גמרא asks how we know that the colors listed in the משנה are impure and the other colors are pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that these are pure and these are impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It wants a source showing which colors of blood belong in the impure group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 proved that pure blood exists, but not which blood it is. The משנה lists certain colors as impure, so the גמרא asks for the source that puts those colors in the impure group and leaves the rest pure.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where (do we know)?
Pure ones
Impure ones

phrases.english: And from where do we know that these are pure,
phrases.notes: These means the colors that the משנה does not list.

phrases.english: and these are impure?
phrases.notes: These means the colors that the משנה does list.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִמַּאי דְּהָנֵי טְהוֹרִין, וְהָנֵי טְמֵאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the conclusion that pure blood exists by asking how to tell pure from impure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the colors in the משנה are impure and other colors are pure.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that blood is red
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings the פסוק about מואב seeing water 'red like blood', which shows that the color of blood is red.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The פסוק says, 'And מואב saw the water red like blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question with a פסוק that connects blood with the color red.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares red water to blood, so we learn that real blood is red. That gives a starting point for which colors count as impure blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Red (plural)
Like blood

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Because the verse says:
'And Moav saw the water
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 3:22

phrases.english: red like blood,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: דְּאָמַר קְרָא: וַיִּרְאוּ מוֹאָב אֶת הַמַּיִם אֲדוּמִּים כַּדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares red water to blood, showing that blood's color is red.

steps.title: Then only red should be impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the פסוק teaches that blood is red, then only red should be impure and nothing else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that blood is red? Then say only red, and nothing more!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אבהו's proof. If blood means red, the other colors in the משנה should not be impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists several colors as impure, not just red. A פסוק that only says 'red like blood' would suggest that red is the one and only impure color, so it cannot be the source for the whole list.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say?
And nothing more

phrases.english: Is this to say that blood is red?
Then say red, and nothing more!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמֵימְרָא דְּדָם אָדוֹם הוּא? אֵימָא אָדוֹם, וְתוּ לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof of step 22 as too narrow.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only points to red, but the משנה makes several colors impure, so the proof would limit impurity to red alone.

steps.title: The double word דמיה gives four types
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו brings a new source: the Torah says 'דמיה' (her bloods) twice. Each plural word means at least two, so there are four types of impure blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: The פסוק says 'her bloods' and 'her bloods', so here there are four.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the challenge with a better source. The plural word 'דמיה' appears twice, giving four kinds of blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'דמיה' is plural, and the smallest plural is two. Since the word appears in two פסוקים, that adds up to four impure types, not just one red color.

keyTerms.meaning: Her bloods: a plural form of the word blood
Here there are four

steps.confusionAlert: The count comes from the plural form: each 'דמיה' counts as two, and two of them make four. It does not mean four separate words.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
The verse says 'her bloods,' 'her bloods,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:7 and ויקרא 20:18. Each plural word counts as at least two.

phrases.english: so here there are four.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: אָמַר קְרָא דָּמֶיהָ דָּמֶיהָ, הֲרֵי כָּאן אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 with a different source that gives more than one color.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source from a plural word in the Torah
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only red blood is impure, based on 'אדומים כדם'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double plural 'דמיה' teaches four types of impure blood.

steps.title: But the משנה lists five
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: the פסוקים give four, but the משנה says there are five impure kinds of blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned 'five' in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the count does not match. The פסוקים give four, while the משנה lists five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו's source fits four colors. The משנה, though, names five impure colors, so one color seems to have no source.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
Five

phrases.english: But we learned 'five' in the Mishnah!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אֲנַן חֲמִשָּׁה תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of four from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation of four types from 'דמיה דמיה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists five impure colors, but the source only covers four.

steps.title: Black is really red that went dark
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that the black blood in the משנה is really red blood that became dark. So there are only four basic types, matching the פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Black is red, but it has been damaged.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא solves the counting problem. Black is not a separate type; it is red blood that has gone dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If black is just spoiled red, then red and black are one basic type. The משנה lists five colors, but they come from four basic types, which fits 'דמיה דמיה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Black
That was damaged, meaning its color went dark

steps.whatToRemember: The impure colors come from 'דמיה' written twice, giving four types. Black is counted as red that went dark, so the משנה's five colors fit the four types.

phrases.english: Rabbi Hanina said:
Black is red,
but it has been damaged.
phrases.notes: Literally 'it was struck': the red color got damaged and turned dark.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁחוֹר אָדוֹם הוּא, אֶלָּא שֶׁלָּקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25 by joining two of the משנה's colors into one type.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining one case: two listed colors are one basic type
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Black is a fifth, separate type with no source in the פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Black is red that went dark, so the five colors are only four basic types.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the idea that black blood is really red
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sets the measure for black blood and says it only turns black after leaving the body, like blood from a wound. This supports רבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: Black means as dark as חרת. Darker than that is impure. Lighter than that, even as dark as blue, is pure. This black blood is not black from the start. It turns black only once it leaves the body, just like blood from a wound turns black after it comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי חנינא's answer from the step before. Black blood is really red blood that darkened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא said black blood is just red blood that went dark. The ברייתא says the same thing in its own words: the blood is not black at first, but turns black once it is taken out, like wound blood. It also gives the exact darkness level for black blood to count as impure.

keyTerms.meaning: A very dark substance used as the measuring color for 'black' blood
Lighter, more faded
A dark blue-ish color
Uprooted, removed (here: when the blood leaves the body)
Blood of a wound

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
phrases.notes: 'This way' means like רבי חנינא in the last step, who said black blood is really red.

phrases.english: Black: like ḥeret;
deeper than that: impure,
lighter, even as dark as blue: pure.

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁחוֹר זֶה לֹא מִתְּחִלָּתוֹ הוּא מַשְׁחִיר,
phrases.english: And this black does not blacken from its beginning,
rather, when it is removed it blackens.
It is comparable to the blood of a wound:
when it is removed, it blackens.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי חנינא's answer from step 26 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's claim that black blood is really red blood that darkened
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא saying black blood only turns black after leaving the body, like wound blood
steps.whatToRemember: Black blood is really red blood that darkened after leaving the body, so it does not count as a separate fifth type.

steps.title: How can בית שמאי add more colors beyond four?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית שמאי, who add fenugreek-water color as impure. It asks: don't they accept the teaching from 'דמיה דמיה' that there are only four types?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: בית שמאי say, even blood like fenugreek water is impure. The גמרא asks: Don't בית שמאי accept 'דמיה' 'דמיה', which gives exactly four types?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה, where בית שמאי add more impure colors. It then challenges them: this seems to go past the four types taught by the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 24, רבי אבהו learned from the two words 'דמיה' that there are four impure types of blood. בית שמאי's extra colors would make more than four. So either בית שמאי disagree with that teaching, or something needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: Water that fenugreek was soaked in (a pale, yellowish color)
They do not hold / do not accept (this teaching)
'Her bloods', a plural word in the פסוק

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
Even like the water of fenugreek.
But don't Beit Shammai hold
"her bloods," "her bloods"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:7 and ויקרא 20:18, the source רבי אבהו used earlier.

phrases.english: Here there are four!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵית לְהוּ לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and tests it against רבי אבהו's four-type teaching.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that fenugreek-water-colored blood is impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים give exactly four types, so adding more colors seems to go against them.

steps.title: Two answers: בית שמאי reject the teaching, or the extra colors are faded red
steps.stepSummary: Either בית שמאי do not accept the four-type teaching, or they do, and their extra colors are just red blood that faded, like רבי חנינא said about black.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say they do not accept it. And if you want, say they do accept it. Didn't רבי חנינא say black is really red, only it was damaged? Here too, these colors are red that was damaged and faded.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two possible answers for בית שמאי. The second one reuses רבי חנינא's idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Answer one: בית שמאי simply disagree with the 'דמיה' teaching and allow more than four types. Answer two: they agree, but the fenugreek and roast-meat colors are not new types. They are red blood that faded, just as black is red that darkened.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say (introduces one of two possible answers)
They do hold / accept (this teaching)
Was damaged, struck (here: the color changed)

phrases.english: If you want, say: they do not hold it,
and if you want, say: they do hold it.
Didn't Rabbi Ḥanina say:
Black is red, only it was damaged?
Here too, it is just that they were damaged.
phrases.notes: He means the fenugreek and roast-meat colors are red blood that faded.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לֵית לְהוּ, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: אִית לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against בית שמאי from step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two alternative answers: rejecting the source, or explaining the extra colors as faded red
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית שמאי's extra colors must be new types beyond the four.
steps.terutzMaskana: Either בית שמאי reject the four-type teaching, or the extra colors are faded red blood and still fit the four.
steps.confusionAlert: The second answer does not say בית שמאי add a new type. It says the extra colors are still red, only faded, so there are still four basic types.

steps.title: Isn't בית הלל's view the same as the תנא קמא's?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית הלל, who say these colors are pure, and asks why they are mentioned, since the תנא קמא already said the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And בית הלל say these are pure. The גמרא asks: That is exactly what the תנא קמא said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last part of this משנה line and asks why בית הלל needed to be mentioned. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא listed only five impure colors, so any other color, like fenugreek water, is pure by his view. בית הלל say these colors are pure too. So it looks like the משנה repeated the same view twice.

keyTerms.meaning: They declare pure
That is the same as
The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel deem them pure.
That is the same as the first tanna!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to בית הלל's part of the same משנה line and questions why it is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's mention of בית הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית הלל's ruling seems identical to the תנא קמא's, so quoting it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: There is a difference between בית הלל and the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 30 by saying that בית הלל and the תנא קמא do not hold exactly the same view. There is a practical difference between them, which the גמרא is about to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a practical difference between them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering the question from step 30 by saying that בית הלל and the תנא קמא really do disagree about something. This line sets up the next move: the גמרא is about to spell out what that difference is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that quoting בית הלל seems pointless if the תנא קמא already said the same thing. The answer is that their views are not identical, so quoting בית הלל adds real information. This line only states that a difference exists; it does not yet say what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: "There is a difference between them": a standard גמרא phrase saying two opinions that look alike actually differ in practice
There is
Between them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop here thinking the answer is finished. אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ is only the opening of the answer. The actual practical difference is explained in the next lines.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
phrases.notes: "Them" means בית הלל and the תנא קמא. The גמרא is about to explain how they differ.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא בֵינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to step 30's question about why בית הלל's ruling is quoted when it seems the same as the תנא קמא's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing two opinions: the views only look identical but differ in a practical case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל and the תנא קמא say exactly the same thing, so quoting בית הלל adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is a practical difference between בית הלל and the תנא קמא, so quoting בית הלל is needed. The details follow in the next lines.
